intro: Lesson 38: Fast-teach 2.7 to 2.9: Shari'ah, Islamic etiquette and the early leaders (Qur'an 5:48, 49:11-13, 9:117). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: 2.8 Set passage: 49:11-13
points: Do not mock others or use offensive nicknames (49:11)
Humanity from one pair, made nations to know one another (49:13)

panels.title: Why it matters
points: Shari'ah guides all of life, not only courts
The early leaders: models of sacrifice and justice

blocks.h: The five categories: my own examples

keywords.def: the way and law given by Allah
analogy: applying a ruling to a similar new case
a successor; a caliph leading the community

questions.q: Explain what 49:11-13 teaches Muslims about how to treat others.
questions.a: Do not mock or insult; avoid suspicion, spying and backbiting; all humans are equal in origin and the most noble is the most righteous, so no racism or pride.

questions.q: Table then paragraph (portal response box): complete the five categories with your own examples; then 'Explain the importance of the early leaders for Muslims', using 9:117 and both Sunni and Shia views.
questions.a: Correct categories and examples. Paragraph: they kept Islam united after the Prophet ﷺ, spread it, compiled the Qur'an; 9:117 praises the Muhajirun and Ansar; Sunni and Shia views stated fairly.

questions.q: Extend: explain how qiyas works with an example.
questions.a: A new case shares the reason ('illah) of an old ruling, so the ruling applies: drugs intoxicate like alcohol, so they are haram.

questions.q: Which is a source of Shari'ah meaning 'agreement of scholars'?
questions.a: A) Ijma'. Ijma' is consensus. Qiyas is analogy; adab is manners; mubah is a category of action.

questions.q: Who was the second caliph for Sunni Muslims?
Think again: where should good laws and manners come from?
questions.a: For Muslims: Allah's guidance in the Qur'an and Sunnah, applied by scholars.
